Users can deploy programmable breakers and switching elements to represent both manual and automatic transfer events. The standard library includes: • Basic three-phase switch models for utility-to-backup source transitions • Logic blocks for emulating status sensing and transfer decision processes • Time delay and sequential switching features. 3.10.2 Additional Model Requirements Custom development might be required to: • Accurately represent the transient switching dynamics, including the difference between a mechanical automatic transfer switch (typical transfer time in seconds) and solid-state static transfer switch (typical transfer time in milliseconds). 15 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Integrate programmable protection coordination to prevent back-feed, ensure source synchronization, and comply with utility interlock requirements. • Implement fault ride-through and seamless load transition during critical events, particularly important for Tier IV and hyperscale data centers with stringent uptime demands. • Design and run test cases for switching under abnormal conditions, such as voltage sags, swells, and faulted source transfer. 16 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Key Metrics/Test Cases for Model Evaluation This section outlines critical metrics and essential test scenarios for validating data center power system models, particularly emphasizing the dynamic behaviors associated with fast-changing load scales, such as AI-driven workload spikes. The metrics align with observations from NERC incident reports (NERC 2025) and recommendations for data center integration to ensure grid stability and reliable operation. The following test metrics ensure that data center models can capture fast transient behaviors, validate protection settings, and assess coordinated DER and load cycling responses under abnormal grid events.
